explanation: Oxygen is only about 21% of dry air, and argon almost 1%. Carbon dioxide, despite its fame, makes up less than a tenth of 1%.

claims.text: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of dry air by volume.
Oxygen, carbon dioxide and argon each make up far less of the air than nitrogen does.
Oxygen makes up about 21% of dry air by volume.
Argon makes up almost 1% of dry air by volume.
Carbon dioxide makes up less than a tenth of 1% of dry air.
